title: One Drop, Blood Red: Why Transition Metals Form Complexes
subject: Chemistry
objective: A complex is a central metal ion bonded to several ligands (anions or neutral molecules) by coordinate bonds, in which the ligand gives both electrons. One drop of KSCN turns pale-yellow Fe³⁺ blood red as [Fe(SCN)(H₂O)₅]²⁺ forms, while the K⁺ from the same drop grabs nothing. Transition-metal ions form far more complexes because they are small (Fe³⁺ 65 pm vs K⁺ 138 pm), highly charged (+3 vs +1) and have d orbitals available for bond formation.

tf.q: K⁺ forms the blood-red complex in the KSCN test for Fe³⁺.
tf.explain: K⁺ is a spectator; the red complex is [Fe(SCN)(H₂O)₅]²⁺.

tf.q: A smaller, more highly charged ion attracts a ligand's lone pair more strongly.
Only transition metals can form complexes.
tf.explain: Others can (Al³⁺, Mg²⁺), but transition metals form far more.

tf.q: [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺ contains four coordinate bonds from N to Cu.
tf.explain: Each NH₃ donates its lone pair on N.

tf.q: In a coordinate bond the metal supplies one electron and the ligand one.

ar.a: Fe³⁺ forms complexes more readily than K⁺.
ar.r: Fe³⁺ is smaller and more highly charged than K⁺.
ar.explain: The correct reason; available d orbitals also help.

ar.r: NH₃ has a lone pair of electrons on nitrogen.
ar.explain: It donates the pair to the metal ion.

short.q: Give three reasons why transition metals form a large number of complexes.
short.solution: Comparatively small size of their ions; high ionic charge; availability of d orbitals for bond formation (NCERT 4.3.11).

short.q: What is a coordinate bond? Explain with [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺.
short.solution: A bond in which both shared electrons come from one atom. In [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺ each NH₃ donates the lone pair on N to Cu²⁺ (N → Cu), giving four coordinate bonds.

short.q: Why does a drop of KSCN turn an Fe³⁺ solution blood red but not a KCl solution?
short.solution: SCN⁻ replaces a water ligand on Fe³⁺ forming the blood-red complex [Fe(SCN)(H₂O)₅]²⁺. K⁺ (big, +1) does not hold the ligand, and KCl has no Fe³⁺.
